outcome: WON on attempt 1, 7 turns, 0 player faints

attempts.note: Weavile dropped to 8/48 from a 4x Mach Punch and was withdrawn; nothing else on my side was ever in danger.

strategy_checks.check: Pawmi opens with Fake Out or a useful Nuzzle on its entry turn
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1 chosen action: battler 1 MOVE_FAKE_OUT -> target 2 (Whimsicott). It did not resolve because my faster Weavile Fake Out flinched Pawmi first; the authored choice was made.

strategy_checks.check: Galarian Farfetch'd attacks immediately instead of paying a setup turn
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 1 chosen action: MOVE_CLOSE_COMBAT -> target 0 (Weavile), which would have been 4x and lethal. No Belly Drum / Focus Energy line exists on this set and none was attempted.

strategy_checks.check: The Leek's guaranteed-critical Leaf Blade / Night Slash lands
strategy_checks.evidence: Farfetch'd (level 13, 40 HP) fainted to a single Whimsicott Moonblast on turn 1 before it ever acted. Its whole authored identity never fired. This drives the level change below.

strategy_checks.check: Clefairy Follow Me redirects the player's single-target attacks
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 2: I aimed Weavile's Icicle Crash and Whimsicott's Moonblast at Pawmi (battler 1). Clefairy used Follow Me, both moves resolved against battler 3, and the Focus Sash Pawmi was preserved at 25/43. Clefairy took 36 damage for its partner.

strategy_checks.check: Clefairy Friend Guard reduces partner damage
strategy_checks.evidence: Arcanine's Extreme Speed into Clefairy on turn 5 did only 10 damage; the Eviolite plus Friend Guard's own defensive contribution is consistent, but Friend Guard's partner-side reduction was not isolated.

strategy_checks.check: Lechonk's Aroma Veil blocks its side's eligible disruption
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 6: Whimsicott used Taunt on Lechonk and the battle text read 'The opposing Lechonk is protected by an aromatic veil'. On turn 5 the same Taunt was instead blocked by Lechonk's Protect, so it took two attempts to isolate.

strategy_checks.check: Helping Hand is used when it beats a direct action
strategy_checks.evidence: Neither Clefairy nor Lechonk ever chose Helping Hand. Both spent their turns on Follow Me, Moonblast, Protect and Body Slam, which were defensible given how fast their partners were dying.
Turn 4: Clefairy, freshly Taunted, withdrew for Lechonk rather than sit through the lock. That is a correct and non-clairvoyant response to a revealed condition.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL - blocked Whimsicott's Taunt, which would have shut off its Helping Hand and Protect for three turns.

ai_observations: Only one opposing Protect in the whole battle and it had a real payoff. No empty, harmful or repetitive guarding in this fight.
Follow Me on turn 2 was the single best decision I saw in this block so far: it read the double-target on the Sash holder and spent a 56 HP body to keep it alive.

level_changes.reason: Brief rule 5: won first try with 0 player faints -> +1 to the weakest members. Farfetch'd-Galar is the floor of this team by two levels (13 against a cap of 14) and the Leek crit engine, which is the trainer's whole authored identity, died to one neutral-ish special attack before acting. It is the lowest-level member, not a Mega or legend, so the 'never the ace first' guard does not apply in the sense the brief intends.
Second lowest offset, and the member that actually earned its keep (Follow Me, Friend Guard) - a level makes the redirection body survive a round longer.

rerun: NOT PERFORMED - the headless ROM cannot be rebuilt in this session. See work/playtest/15-MARLENE/receipt.json for the toolchain detail.
cooler_note: Mostly yes already. The two bodyguard modes (Follow Me + Friend Guard versus Aroma Veil) are genuinely distinct and both showed up in play, which is more than most teams in this block managed. The weak link is the concept-versus-level mismatch: a guaranteed-critical Leek attacker is a memorable idea that is authored two levels below the cap, so the player never meets it. Suggestion for a later pass, not applied here: lead Farfetch'd-Galar behind Clefairy's Follow Me rather than beside Pawmi, so the bodyguard buys the crit attacker its turn - that is the same package the trainer already owns, arranged so the payoff is visible.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem. All four members, abilities, items and moves resolved correctly.
not_finished: The Leek guaranteed-critical line and Helping Hand were never exercised. The +1/+1 calibration has not been retested in a rebuilt ROM.
